newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo shells hit old Mobutu camp over the river.
newsitem.headline: Congo shells hit old Mobutu camp over the river.

text.p: Shells fired by one of Congo's warring factions in Brazzaville slammed on Monday into a military camp over the river frontier in former Zaire, witnesses and officials said.

"Seven shells hit Camp Tshatshi. We could tell precisely where they were fired from," Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha said in an interview, declining to identify the suspects but calling the incident unacceptable.
Witnesses said there were no casualties.
Karaha called in Western ambassadors to inform them and said new President Laurent Kabila's cabinet would hold an emergency meeting.

He said this was the sixth time that shells had fallen in or near Kinshasa, capital of the newly renamed Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazzaville's twin city on the other bank of the mighty Congo river.
It was unclear if the shelling was deliberately targeted across the frontier.
Camp Tshatshi, infamous to locals as a base for ousted Zairean leader Mobutu Sese Seko's hated presidential guard, also housed his official Kinshasa residence.
He was toppled by rebel leader Kabila a month ago. Tshatshi is now a military camp for Kabila's army.
The shells fell during a 90-minute artillery duel on Monday between Congo's pro- and anti-president factions that weakened but did not kill off a six-day-old ceasefire.

Brazzaville was carved into opposing sectors and no man's lands by clashes that flared on June 5 when President Pascal Lissouba tried to disarm a militia run by his predecessor and political foe, Denis Sassou Nguesso.
